The basal metabolic rate of the Mexican spiny pocket mouse, Liomys irroratus, has been measured under controlled laboratory conditions. This value, representing the maximum basal metabolic rate, falls within the range expected for a heteromyid rodent of moderate body size. In terms of reproductive output, females typically give birth to litters ranging from 2 to 8 pups. The maximum reproductive rate, observed under favorable conditions in captivity, is approximately 4 litters per year [F_R_i = 4 litters per year], of 2 to 8 pups per litter [N_R_i = of 2 to 8 pups per litter]. The reproductive data were collected from a colony maintained at a constant ambient temperature of 35.2 °C [T = 35.2 °C].

Estimates of neonatal body mass for Liomys irroratus are derived from observations on the related species Heteromys salvini, given the paucity of direct measurements for the spiny pocket mouse. Newborn pups have a wet weight of approximately 1.9 grams [Wwb = approximately 1.9 grams], a diminutive starting size for an altricial mammal that will undergo substantial growth. Adult body size exhibits a pronounced sexual dimorphism in this species. This is a relatively extended lifespan for a small rodent and is consistent with the slower life-history pace often observed in heteromyid species. The gestation period, an important component of reproductive timing, has been estimated from the closely related species Heteromys salvini. At a controlled temperature of 35.3 °C [T = 35.3 °C], the gestation time is approximately 27 days [tg = approximately 27 days]. This relatively brief gestation is characteristic of small-bodied mammals that produce altricial young requiring an extended period of postnatal care.

At this point, the suckling juveniles, which have been entirely dependent on their mother's milk, make the dietary transition to solid food and achieve nutritional independence.
